text.p: Nigerian shares ended lower again on Friday, and traders said there was no end in sight to the weaker trend.
The all-share index closed 8458.02 against 8462.02 on Thursday.
Traders said bearish sentiment ruling the market would probably persist in the coming week as the economic situation in Nigeria still appeared gloomy.
"Not much productive activity is going on here," one said. "The government decision not to release funds for the last two quarters is hurting business."
Business executives have also spoken of rising production costs, fuelled by lingering fuel scarcity in Africa's leading crude oil exporter.
They said investors were wary of buying shares until the situation improves.
Continued dumping saw the shares of PZ Industries slump 15 kobo to 28.30 naira on Friday. The conglomerate is the most capitalised firm in the market.
Union Bank fell 20 kobo to 10.80 naira while West African Portland Cement Company shed five kobo to end at 62.25 naira.
Other blue chips posting losses were Cadbury and Coca-Cola bottler, the Nigerian Bottling Company, both down 10 kobo at 35.80 naira and 54.20 naira, respectively.
Oil shares Agip was 17.50 naira, down 50 kobo, and Total closed 20 kobo down at 58.20 naira.
Food company Nestle continued to gain, strengthening by one naira to 51.00 naira.
Brewer Guinness edged up by five kobo to 6.90 naira because investors considered the price cheap.

United Bank for Africa added 15 kobo to 11.30 naira for the same reason. Wema Bank, up 10 kobo at 3.45 naira, and NAL Merchant Bank, three kobo stronger at 8.25 naira, put the banking sector in a bullish position.
